references.text: Moses and Aaron throw the staff before Pharaoh, and it becomes a snake. Pharaoh's magicians do the same with their sorcery.
God commands Moses to grab the snake by its tail, and it turns back into a staff.
Aaron performs the signs that the Lord had shown Moses, including the staff that became a snake.
Moses makes a bronze snake at the Lord's command. The snake as a symbol of both judgment and salvation.
The snake (נָחָשׁ) is introduced for the first time in the Bible as a cunning creature.
Jesus refers to Moses lifting up the snake in the wilderness, linking it to his own crucifixion.
The performance of the miracle before Pharaoh (7:10) directly fulfills the instruction given to Moses in the wilderness (4:3).
The bronze snake in Numbers 21:9 is a theological response to the snake motif; while Moses fled from the snake (4:3), the people must look at it to live.
The verse contains the direct prophetic instruction that is carried out in chapter 4 and later in chapter 7.
